newsitem.title: DUBAI: Last minute plan change saves Saudi from jet crash.
newsitem.headline: Last minute plan change saves Saudi from jet crash.

text.p: A last-minute change in plan saved a Saudi airline security man from the mid-air collision over India in which 350 people are believed killed, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

The London-based Arabic-language Asharq Al-Awsat said Bassam Zinimal, a Saudi from the Islamic holy city of Mecca, "had excused himself at the last minute from travelling, thus escaping the disaster".
It said Zinimal telephoned his family in Saudi Arabia after the crash on Tuesday night to tell them he had not been on the flight and was safe.
It did not say why the man, who it reported was a member of an anti-terrorism security team on the plane, missed the flight.

Five Saudi security men are among those believed killed when the Saudi Boeing 747, shortly after taking off from New Delhi, collided with an incoming Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter at a height of 15,000 feet (4,570 metres).
Indian officials said there were 312 people, including 23 crew, on the Saudi flight SV 763, bound for Dhahran and Jeddah.
